continuity.transport: Meenakshi drives her own car to the hospital on Jan 2 and keeps car throughout; Avi/Yash/Aditi share a realistic four-seat trip with seatbelts. No unplanned bike ride or three on a two-wheeler.

Hospital Chotu-role is Naveen (22), society Chotu-role Babloo (23); their roles and backstories stay distinct.
continuity.pendingMysteries: Previous unauthorized locker access remains reader-only; Meenakshi noticed a small change at 13:10 on Jan 1, set things in place and soon forgot about it. No photo, complaint or ongoing anxiety. Earlier changing-room incident remains unknown to her; Mohan's hidden interest and Nikhil's surprise are separate unresolved strands.
continuity.interaction: Adult fictional romance/innuendo; private admiration separated from Meenakshi's knowledge. A physical moment never proves consent to additional intimacy. Workplace hierarchy and patient context respected.

timeline.title: Three Younger Colleagues
beats: Serious ward work first: Meenakshi reviews a case; Avi is openly confident; Yash checks figures; Aditi handles a difficult follow-up independently.
Aditi (24) is their same-age female peer: witty and observant, not a prop or a presumed romantic participant.
At the file handoff, Avi compliments Meenakshi's composure; Yash is quiet but attentive; Aditi notices their different responses.
Meenakshi says thank you professionally and does not allow patient care to become flirting.
dialogue: Avi, file ke numbers pe bhi utna hi focus kar lo jitna apni one-liners pe.
Report bhi dekh raha hoon, Doctor sahiba ka confidence bhi notice kar raha hoon.
Pehle report pass karo. Compliments ki marking baad mein.
notes: Avi/Yash are work duo, not biological twins; Aditi is 24 and has independent clinical tasks.

timeline.title: A Compliment, a Glance, and a Wink
beats: After rounds the four adults pause for tea: flirting is outside patient-facing spaces.
Avi's compliment has a plausible double meaning; Meenakshi outwardly deflects but privately feels briefly flattered by attention from younger adult colleagues.
Yash quietly notices her relieved smile and evening outfit beneath the open white coat; no intrusive gaze is endorsed.
Avi catches Yash's glance, taps his shoulder and winks; Yash blushes, Aditi spots the exchange and teases both.
Meenakshi catches part of the exchange; the reader sees her private pleased-but-cautious reaction distinct from the trio's private interpretations.
dialogue: Aaj aapke observation rounds khatam hue, ya hum abhi bhi examination mein hain?
Tum log symptoms se zyada double meanings produce kar rahe ho.
Main toh observation likh bhi nahi raha.
Haan, aur isi liye tumhara face sab bata raha hai.

arc.physical: Visible expression, eye contact and shoulder tap between peers
arc.emotional: Momentary blush and warmth; not a promise

notes: Use spoken vs reader-only reactions separately; jokes are mutually responsive, not a license for touching.

timeline.title: Naveen — The Missing Annexure
beats: Chotu-equivalent in the hospital is Naveen (22), an admin assistant already present in 1 Jan M06; not a newly invented stranger.
Introduce his established function and familiarity through reliable shift-sheet work; any family hardship, tuition or nickname backstory is only a proposal until accepted.
He delivers the senior-review annexure, discovers one page is missing, offers to retrieve it and returns after a short interval.
Meenakshi nicknames his speed 'express service'; his private impression is that her encouragement feels personal, while she regards it as friendly senior-colleague warmth.
The missing-document-and-second-visit mechanism is separate from Babloo's society delivery.
dialogue: Naveen, annexure mein page three kahan hai? Invisible ink?
Scan room mein reh gaya. Five minutes, ma'am.
Express service ke saath accuracy bhi included honi chahiye.

arc.physical: Passing a file, hands remain respectful
arc.psychological: One-sided first impression; Meenakshi not aware of any crush

notes: This is first focused Naveen introduction, NOT his first-ever appearance; no private locker access for Naveen.

timeline.title: Avi Requests the Ride
beats: Official health-camp vendor samples must be verified on Meenakshi's already planned route toward home.
Avi initiates the lift request. His stated logistical reason is genuine, but he privately hopes to spend time with her; no false fuel story is forced.
Meenakshi checks the address, agrees because she is already driving, and invites Aditi along for the supplies checklist.
Yash is assigned directions; Aditi handles paperwork. Professional hierarchy, boundaries and freedom to decline remain explicit.
dialogue: Doctor, vendor route mein hai. Agar aap drop kar dein toh cartons verify ho jayenge.
Sirf isliye ki mera route same hai. Aditi, list tumhare paas hogi?

arc.psychological: Avi sets up the ride expecting more attention

notes: Car belongs to Meenakshi; exact vendor address not canonized; trip is off-site team work, no patient transport.

timeline.title: Who Was Watching Whom?
beats: Meenakshi walks ahead carrying her bag and a lightweight supply register; three younger peers follow a short distance.
Avi privately admires her confident walk and fitted but everyday departure outfit. Yash also notices; admiration is kept as a private POV, not an invitation.
Avi notices Yash's glance and gives the same private shoulder-tap and wink mechanism; Yash blushes. Aditi sees them and quietly calls out their competitiveness.
Meenakshi glances back, notices their expressions and feels a brief internal blush before returning to the practical task.
The parking-lot walking tableau is retained as an independent beat, not collapsed into 'they flirt'.
dialogue: Tum dono files ke saath-saath expressions bhi coordinate karte ho?
Kya secret meeting chal rahi hai?

arc.physical: Walking, noticed glances, peer-only shoulder tap
arc.emotional: She feels briefly attractive and slightly self-conscious
arc.psychological: Private rivalry shown before vehicle seating

notes: Visual body-language admiration is reader-only; no explicit body-part fixation or stalking.

timeline.title: The Unexpected Front Seat
beats: Avi requested the ride and expects the front passenger seat; Yash already has navigation open.
Meenakshi asks Yash to navigate from the front; Avi and Aditi sit in back with folders, preserving all four seatbelts.
Avi conceals disappointment; Yash quietly enjoys the unexpected position but does not use it to intrude.
Aditi quietly teases Avi; Meenakshi notices through the rear-view mirror only at a safe stop, never while navigating a turn.
Light, mutual double entendre about 'front-row attention' and medical evaluations continues without breaking safe driving.
dialogue: Yash, GPS tumhare paas hai toh front mein baitho. Avi, Aditi ke saath files check karo.
Request meri, front row kisi aur ki. Interesting system hai.
Main bas directions de raha hoon.
notes: No three-person motorcycle ride; safe four-adult car trip.

timeline.title: The Narrow Step
beats: At the supplier bay Aditi confirms seals; Avi checks inventory; Yash helps Meenakshi inspect a labelled carton.
A trolley passes across a narrow step. She asks to steady herself on his forearm, and he agrees; he supports her upper arm for two seconds while she steps across.
Close proximity and brief natural contact create surprise for both; they separate as soon as steady. No uninvited waist hold and no claim that silence means consent.
Avi sees the closeness and later privately replays the moment. Aditi redirects the group to the actual supply count.
Meenakshi's inner reaction is a small, surprising awareness of Yash's considerate behaviour, layered with professional caution.
dialogue: Step narrow hai. Main tumhara arm hold kar loon?
Of course. Careful, trolley aa rahi hai.
Count complete. Do boxes, seals intact.
Aur safety audit bhi complete, lagta hai.

arc.physical: Asked-and-accepted forearm steady + upper-arm support, then release
arc.psychological: Avi witnesses a moment he expected for himself

notes: Original motorcycle grip cannot logically transfer to car; use credible contact at loading step, not a contrived embrace.

timeline.location: Vendor to colleague drop-off to society
timeline.title: Four Different Memories
beats: Meenakshi drops the three colleagues at a suitable public transit point, then drives herself back to society with her car.
Avi jokes about losing the front seat; Aditi responds that the work was completed and has no patience for exaggerated rivalry.
Yash keeps his thoughts private. Meenakshi recalls his calm warning at the narrow step, not an imagined romantic promise.
The group separates clearly by 16:35–16:40. Meenakshi arrives home at about 17:00.
dialogue: Agli baar front seat ke liye application dunga.
Application reject karne ka right mere paas hai.

arc.physical: All safely separated after short ride
arc.psychological: Different POV memories; no secret romance

notes: Do not imply Meenakshi drove them to their homes or that the trio lives in Gulmohar Heights.

timeline.title: The Other Pair of Brothers
beats: Meenakshi, now at society with her car parked, checks the camp register and finds Uday and Utkarsh setting up a lightweight noticeboard.
Uday resumes confident innuendo using a health-checkup metaphor; Meenakshi banters back instead of recoiling.
Utkarsh makes an understated observation; she remembers his 1 January comment about being noticed, and privately smiles.
A banner clip slips; she hands Utkarsh a clip and their fingers brush briefly during the handoff, followed by a normal, unhurried separation.
Uday sees that she focuses on Utkarsh's answer, and his playful sibling competitiveness increases. Do NOT stage a second vehicle ride the same evening.
dialogue: Doctor sahiba, hum dono ki attention ka follow-up kab hoga?
Tumhari attendance check karungi. Attention ke extra marks nahi.
Mujhe toh kal ki observation yaad hai. Doctor ne khud hume notice kiya tha.
Tumhari memory ka treatment mushkil hoga.

arc.physical: Brief incidental fingers-at-clip touch, no claimed intimacy
arc.emotional: Familiar laughter and mildly increased awareness
arc.psychological: Yash's quietness and Utkarsh's quietness form an internal comparison

notes: Uday/Utkarsh are actual twins, not hospital colleagues. Scene contrasts office dynamic rather than duplicating ride.

timeline.title: Babloo — The First Box
beats: Society Chotu-equivalent Babloo (23), an established pharmacy pickup helper already recognised in EP01 and EP02; not Naveen under another name.
He carries a sealed heavy pharmacy-supply box, is proud to help, and respectfully asks where to put it.
Meenakshi checks items with the bill, thanks him, and gives practical lifting advice.
One labelled packet is missing. Babloo apologizes, contacts the supplier and volunteers to return shortly.
Reader sees Babloo's quiet admiration for her kindness; Meenakshi trusts his work but does not infer romantic interest.
dialogue: Didi, heavy carton hai. Entry par rakh doon?
Haan. Peeth seedhi rakho, hero banne ke chakkar mein injury mat kar lena.
Aapke camp ka samaan hai; complete launga.
Bill mein ek packet missing hai. Pehle supplier se verify karo.

arc.physical: Practical box handoff, no deliberate intimate touch
arc.psychological: Second Chotu-lane begins without conflating helper with hospital admin

notes: Duration of their acquaintance is not yet canonized; no invented hardship, and no child in attraction framing.

timeline.title: The Smile She Cannot Explain
beats: Meenakshi changes into comfortable home attire and organizes camp documents; she chooses her own privacy, independently of who will ring.
She mentally compares Avi's boldness, Yash's care, Uday's humor, Utkarsh's observation, and the practical help of Naveen/Babloo without treating all attention as romance.
Her husband Nikhil remains emotionally important; the Jan1 private surprise is an unresolved strand, not silently declared completed.
A message says Babloo is bringing the missing item. She plans to verify the bill at the doorway, not assume a visitor may enter.

arc.emotional: Brief flattering thrill followed by reflective restraint
arc.psychological: Distinct relationship strands and reader-only secrets kept separate

notes: Mohan's Jan1 pouch secret and the hospital locker mystery remain unresolved; no child is placed in sexual subplots.

timeline.title: The Second Knock
beats: The second doorbell rings while Meenakshi is checking the inventory and getting ready to answer.
She checks who is outside, adjusts her shawl for her own comfort, and asks Babloo to confirm the missing label through the door.
Reader knows Babloo returned to complete the task; Meenakshi is not granted knowledge of any hidden feelings.
End at the door opening/hand-off threshold. The next episode can continue the same evening before any next-morning transition.
dialogue: Ji didi. Seal bhi intact hai.

arc.psychological: Second-visit cliffhanger connects original mechanism to her real routine

notes: Do not rewrite 1 Jan EP02; this is 2 Jan evening. Original EP04 resumes the same day; only later goes into the following morning.
